extracted.intended_audience: USPTO-registered patent practitioners, patent attorneys/agents, and legal professionals involved in USPTO disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_short: USPTO professional conduct for patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and sanctions governing the professional conduct of patent practitioners before the USPTO, including duties to consult and communicate with clients, avoid acquiring adverse interests, properly terminate representation, and comply with disciplinary sanctions and remedial requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct set forth at 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101 through 11.901.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any registered patent attorney/practitioner must follow these rules when practicing before the Office; the Final Order treats violations of these rules as the basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction for disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary proceedings, Final Orders, and settlement agreements are taken under these statutory and regulatory authorities and can be the basis for sanctions and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.102(a) — abide by client's decisions concerning objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must abide by a client's decisions concerning the objectives of the representation; filing an application without the client's knowledge or consent violates § 11.102(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from the Order: filing the provisional application 'without the knowledge or consent of Mr. [client]' is cited as a violation. Practitioners must obtain client consent on core objectives before acting.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(2) — reasonable consultation about means
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must reasonably consult with clients about the means by which the clients' objectives are to be accomplished; failing to adequately consult prior to filing violates § 11.104(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order cites failure to consult 'prior to the filing of the provisional application' as a violation. Consultation includes explaining options and planned actions and receiving client input when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.105(b) — communicate scope of representation
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must adequately communicate the scope of the representation to the client; failing to do so violates § 11.105(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order finds inadequate communication of scope (e.g., no written representation agreement and actions creating reasonable belief of representation). Clear communication (preferably in writing) of scope and limits of representation is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.108(a) — avoid acquiring adverse interests; obtain informed consent
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may not knowingly acquire an interest adverse to a client; naming oneself as a co-inventor in a client's patent application without obtaining informed consent violates § 11.108(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order explicitly: 'knowingly acquiring an interest adverse to her client by naming herself as a co-inventor ... without obtaining informed consent from her client.' Practitioners must obtain informed, written consent (and consider conflict rules) before acquiring any interest adverse to a client.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.116 — give proper notice of termination of representation
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must give proper notice when the attorney-client relationship is terminated; failure to provide notice when clients reasonably believe representation continues violates § 11.116.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order notes Respondent 'asserts that the representation ceased at various points prior to November 1, 2017, and the clients had reasonable belief that the attorney-client relationship continued, and no notice of termination was given.' Practitioners should communicate termination clearly to clients to avoid confusion and continuing obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing and filing patent applications is practice before the Office (creates Rule obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparing a patent application in which another party is named as an inventor constitutes practice before the Office and creates obligations under the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order states Respondent now understands that preparing such an application is 'practice before the Office' and thus triggers ethical obligations. Practitioners should treat such preparation as regulated practice and follow applicable rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of written representation/fee agreements (recommended practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: The matter involved representation without a written representation agreement and the CLE remedy includes 'usage of written fee agreements' as a primary subject; written agreements are therefore recommended to clarify scope and fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires CLE including 'usage of written fee agreements' — implying that written fee/representation agreements are a best practice to avoid disputes about scope, fees, or termination. While not cited as a specific violated regulation in isolation, absence of a written agreement was a relevant factual circumstance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial/mitigating conduct (refunds and acknowledgement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent refunded funds to the client and acknowledged understanding that certain actions constitute practice before the Office; such remedial actions are noted as additional considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refund to the client and acceptance of responsibility/education are treated as mitigating factors when determining sanctions and compliance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: public reprimand and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is publicly reprimanded; the OED Director will electronically publish the Final Order in the OED FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication language is prescribed (materially consistent notice); public reprimand is an available disciplinary sanction and will be made publicly accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: probation and CLE compliance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is placed on a twenty-four month probationary period; within twelve months must take and complete at least eight hours of Continuing Legal Education (CLE) with primary subjects including general legal ethics, legal ethics as it relates to patent practitioners, usage of written fee agreements, or law office management; must file an affidavit and documentation corroborating completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probation conditions are concrete: timing (within 12 months), minimum hours (8), subject matter, and proof to be filed with the OED Director. Failure to comply may lead to further action under the enforcement procedure described in the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement procedure during probation (Order to Show Cause and possible suspension)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes the respondent failed to comply with the Agreement, Final Order, or any disciplinary rule during probation, the OED Director may issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to respondent, grant 15 days to respond, and, after consideration, deliver materials to the USPTO Director to request immediate suspension for up to one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure steps: (1) OED issues Order to Show Cause, (2) send to respondent at record address, (3) 15-day response period, (4) if noncompliance determination persists, OED forwards the Order to Show Cause, respondent's response, and supporting argument/evidence to the USPTO Director and requests suspension up to one year. If suspended, a review does not stay the suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects on future proceedings and waiver of certain appeal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of this disciplinary proceeding may be used by the Office in future complaints or proceedings and to rebut statements by respondent; respondent waived rights to seek reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56 and review under § 11.57 and waived other appeals or challenges to the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary records serve as aggravating factors or evidence in future matters; waiver of appeal/reconsideration rights is a condition of the settlement/Final Order. Parties bear their own costs.
